executiveSummary: GM0232's identity, 2025 boundary, province and Veiligheidsregio Noord- en Oost-Gelderland assignment are coherent. Fresh CBS gives 33,469 residents; 29 neighbourhood rows sum to 33,475 (+6, +0.018%), and model detail reconciles local allocation to the municipal control. All ten canonical scenarios execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across Power, Water, Drainage, Gas, Telecom, Mobility, Facilities and Supply; exact-zero input, finite bounds, selected-layer invariance, arithmetic causal closure and the current restriction of unqualified NWB roads to Mobility and explicitly assumed road-logistics/Supply pass. Release is nevertheless correction-required. A controlled source in official BRT mixed forest near Gortel reaches direct-fire intensity 0.340431 at T+11, but its containing Buitengebied Vaassen ranks 23rd of 29 while urban Heggerenk ranks first. The generic river screen sustains 3.142642 m, about 19,000-20,167 affected population-equivalent and only 19.6% Drainage/27.7% Mobility through T+72 without selecting an IJssel defence failure, water level, connected LIWO footprint, arrival or recession; Kern Oene ranks 25th despite the municipality identifying IJssel influence, seepage, dikes and local water-system constraints there. Pluvial, coastal, heat and wildfire reuse exactly the same complete neighbourhood order. Compound forcing falls from severity 0.809967 to 0.246330 while all eight services worsen, affected population-equivalent rises from 21,411 to 21,657 and recovery remains zero. Six logical roads and 21 GTFS stops do not establish evacuation, forest access, hospital reachability or route state. Public sources identify 143 water assets, Liander/Vitens/Ziggo territories, one grid-capacity sample, 79 antenna sites, 31 education uses and no local RIVM emergency department, but geometry, territories and registers are context—not physical topology, current capacity, operation or restoration. Current observations, warning absence and drought measures are not scenario forecasts; no-data is never zero or safe.

evidenceSources.title: Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025, table 86165NED, OData API
supports: The fresh official municipality row identifies GM0232 Epe and gives 33,469 residents, density 214 per square kilometre, 9,046 residents aged 65+, 4,675 one-person households and 14,569 households.

The 29 generated neighbourhood rows sum to 33,475 residents (+6, +0.018%), 9,040 residents aged 65+, 4,675 one-person households and 14,570 households. These small differences retain CBS randomized-rounding, suppression and incomplete-value semantics.
The official age-65-plus share is 27.0%, which is material to heat, evacuation, communication, care and supply planning but is not itself an incident-time needs register.
CBS OData is machine-readable under CC BY 4.0. CBS describes quarterly additions for the 2025 table; null, suppressed, rounded and incomplete values remain publisher semantics and never become zero.

Simulation role is official demographic/context and an allocation control only. Registered residence is not incident-time presence, visitor exposure, evacuation demand, care need or utility-customer topology.

evidenceSources.title: CBS full municipality geometry and national land-cover, settlement and transport reference services
evidenceSources.edition: 2025 boundary; current generated BAG, BRT, NWB, ProRail and GTFS reference editions
supports: Fresh full-resolution GM0232 is a one-component MultiPolygon with one exterior ring, 2,363 positions, validity 1 January through 31 December 2025 and bbox [5.840830924100907, 52.25580705396725, 6.094857433275154, 52.39843712018272]. The generated centre [5.967725232909205, 52.33051875253281] lies inside.

The regional bundle contains four districts, 29 neighbourhoods, four BAG places (Emst, Epe, Oene and Vaassen) and 24 settlement labels: 19 buurtschappen, one gehucht and four woonkernen; no BAG-place centre mismatch is reported.

Six NWB logical boundary routes are present: A50 toward Apeldoorn and Heerde, N792 toward Voorst, N309 toward Elburg, N795 toward Nunspeet and N794 toward Heerde. There is no ProRail station inside the boundary and there are 21 GTFS stop areas.

BRT Top10NL feature a8436c67-71ba-5500-b43c-b030f600c9dc is mixed forest near Gortel inside BU02320211 Buitengebied Vaassen, with source actuality 1 January 2024 and registration 1 June 2025. It supplies the reproducible controlled source coordinate [5.881675887977473, 52.30926841411657].

BRT Top10NL OGC Features is nationwide 1:10,000 reference geometry, CC BY 4.0 and published with annual dataset cadence plus per-feature dates. AHN4 DTM is available at https://service.pdok.nl/rws/ahn/wms/v1_0 as 0.5 m CC0 terrain from 2020-2022 acquisition. These are land-cover/elevation context, not fuel moisture, flame perimeter or live flood depth.

CBS boundary OGC is half-yearly/CC BY 4.0; BAG is daily/Public Domain Mark 1.0; NWB is monthly/CC0 1.0; ProRail reference geometry is manually refreshed/CC0 1.0. Generated OVapi GTFS is a 30 August-12 December 2026 best-effort feed under free-use terms without an SLA.

Reference geometry supplies candidate location and Mobility/Supply connectivity only. It never proves passability, measured throughput, occupancy, hazard exposure, utility topology, service state or restoration.

evidenceSources.title: Beleidsplan Klimaatadaptatie 2025-2030 and municipal water-nuisance information
evidenceSources.edition: Climate-adaptation policy 2025-2030; current municipal pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The plan records the Verloren Beek leaving its banks after heavy rain in February 2022 and the first groundwater-use restrictions during drought in August 2022. It uses a 74 mm in one hour climate-stress event and identifies street-, brook-, groundwater- and water-system mechanisms rather than a common spatial seed.

Named water constraints include Schotweg, full Epe-centre ponds, Verloren Beek/Papenstraat and its culvert, Gelriaweg, Oosterhof/Jonasweg, and in Oene the Horthoekerweg pump capacity, recurrent high groundwater influenced by the IJssel, constrained water systems, IJssel-dike seepage and limited Nieuwe Wetering inflow.

The plan describes wildfire as one of Epe's most urgent risks because forests contain or adjoin homes, roads, care facilities and many holiday parks. It specifically calls for evacuation analysis of two holiday-park clusters and records 2024 awareness meetings at Tongeren and Gortel.

The municipality reports approximately one quarter of residents are 65+ and notes that many older residents occupy homes not adapted to heat; its local heat plan is a communication mechanism, not a measured contact, cooling or care-capacity state.

The municipal water page explains that infiltration, saturated ground, paving, sewer capacity, ditches, brooks and wadis vary street by street and separates municipal sewer/road/ditch duties from water-board main-watercourse and level duties.

These fixed HTML/PDF publications have policy/event-driven revision and no declared standard reusable-data licence, API, WMS/WFS or guaranteed refresh cadence. The best correction input is the municipality's native versioned stress-test raster and hotspot register, requested with event definition, units, valid edition, licence and explicit NoData semantics; the PDF alone must not drive simulation.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Vallei en Veluwe / Het Waterschapshuis / PDOK
evidenceSources.title: Epe water-system evidence and IMWA/DAMO public OGC services
evidenceSources.edition: Beaver-risk report 11 April 2025; current drought pages and HWH snapshot inspected September 2026
supports: In September 2023 a beaver burrow caused a breach in the canal embankment at Epe between Oenerweg and Vemderweg. Apeldoorns Kanaal water flowed into the Grift, the canal fell 25 cm and a cycle path collapsed and closed; the Grift carried the flow so this event caused no inundation. A March 2024 survey of 12 km found 25 burrows, ten deeper than two metres.

The deployment's national HWH/PDOK point-in-polygon screen returns 143 objects inside GM0232: 132 weirs, four surface-water pumps, five sewer pumps, one sluice and RWZI Epe. Named examples include pumps De Brand, Emsterbroek, Vossenbroek and Papenkamp; sewer pumps Vaassen, Epe, Dorpsebeek, Oene and Emst; and Vaassense Sluis.

HWH OGC APIs at https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-kunstwerken-imwa/ogc/v2 and https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 are machine-readable under CC BY-SA 4.0. The national aggregation is explicitly partial and completeness varies by water board; service-specific updates are weekly or contributor-dependent.

For water-defence and catchment corrections, HWH also publishes weekly CC BY-SA IMWA OGC collections at https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-keringen-imwa/ogc/v1, https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-zoneringen-imwa/ogc/v1 and https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterbeheergebieden-imwa/ogc/v1. Registration, status and geometry do not prove current defence strength, gate/pump position, storage, flow or operational availability.

The water board's 2026 drought liveblog is current observed/operational context: low IJssel levels constrained inflow to Apeldoorns Kanaal, a temporary pump was used at Terwolde and abstraction restrictions changed over time. It is updated event-by-event and has no declared machine API or reuse licence; it is not an arbitrary heat exercise or T+72 forecast.

Simulation role is versioned hydrologic, defence and wastewater context. Live levels, breaches, control state, flow, backup power and restoration require Waterinfo or authorized water-board feeds; absent state stays Unknown.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025-2028 and annexes
supports: VNOG records 7,109 hectares of nature area in Epe and identifies the Veluwe's extensive forest/heath, recreation, care facilities, homes, businesses and vital infrastructure as a major nature-fire setting.

Its regional profile includes river flooding, nature fire, extreme weather, prolonged heat/drought, electricity, drinking water, telecom/ICT, cyber and dangerous-goods mechanisms and describes cooperation with municipalities, water boards, Rijkswaterstaat, ProRail, Liander, Vitens, Gasunie and KPN.

The nature-fire scenario describes prolonged drought/heat, wind-driven spread, risk to residents, recreation users and responders, regional coordination, operational information, specialist equipment, training and recovery. These mechanisms require an explicit source/perimeter, current weather, access, water and resource state.
The risk profile notes regional recreation and cross-boundary effects; registered municipal residents therefore do not exhaust Epe's incident-time exposure.

The fixed risk-profile/crisis publications follow governance cadence, broadly four years, and expose no live machine resource, capacity or action feed and no standard reuse licence. They support scenario selection and mechanisms, never activated crews, shelters, hospital acceptance, passability or restoration.

evidenceSources.title: KNMI Data Platform observations, radar, forecasts and weather warnings
evidenceSources.edition: Deployment observations at 2 September 2026 23:30 UTC and warning issue/fallback time 21:36 UTC
supports: The public-context snapshot contains no fixed KNMI weather station in Epe; the nearest listed station to the municipal reference point is Heino about 22.9 km away. The 10-minute observations are sparse points, not a continuous municipal field.
The snapshot carries no issued Gelderland warning for its 48-hour window. This means no warning in that issue, not zero storm, rain, heat, snow/ice or wildfire danger at a separate scenario time.

KNMI makes 10-minute station observations, five-minute radar, continuous 48-hour warnings and forecast products available through the Open Data API, Notification Service, EDR API and WMS as applicable under CC BY 4.0.

KNMI warnings extend at most 48 hours; possible dangerous weather may be indicated farther ahead with uncertainty. A T+72 operational state therefore needs an explicit forecast product/issue and cannot be inferred from a current warning or station reading.

Simulation role should be timestamped observation/forecast forcing and validation only when aligned to the exercise. Observation time, issue time, valid time, spatial support, revision and missing-variable semantics must be preserved.

evidenceSources.title: LIWO flood scenarios, Waterinfo measurements and current road situations
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO 2025.1.6; deployment Waterinfo and NDW snapshots of 2 September 2026
supports: LIWO contains professional flood-scenario layers for Dutch crisis preparation, including depth and arrival products. WMCN/IPLO warns that correct interpretation requires water-manager expertise; a named scenario/breach and version must be selected rather than treating a centre-distance transform as local depth.

LIWO provides professional map/download/WMS routes, but account/access and dataset-specific reuse terms need verification at integration. Releases are versioned and irregular; 2025.1.6 is listed on the official page. No-data cells, scenario non-coverage and dry cells must remain distinct.

Waterinfo exposes public latest water-level/discharge point observations, generally every ten minutes, under CC0 unless a component states otherwise. The generated snapshot assigns no observation point to GM0232; absence is not zero level/discharge or safety and points are not hydraulic surfaces.

NDW's CC0 DATEX II current-situations feed is machine-readable and frequently published. The deployment snapshot has no record assigned to GM0232; supplier validation varies and no record does not prove all six modeled corridors, local roads or forest access are passable at scenario time.

The RWS Klimaateffectatlas 70 mm/2 h scenario WMS at https://geo.rijkswaterstaat.nl/services/ogc/gdr/klimaat_effect_atlas/ows is CC0 and machine-readable, with catalogue update 5 August 2026. It is scenario context rather than observation and should be intersected with full geometry and compared with Epe's own 74 mm/1 h stress-test definition.

evidenceSources.publisher: Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / RIVM / DUO / KVK-PDOK
evidenceSources.title: Public provider, grid-planning, telecom, care, education and government-service context
evidenceSources.edition: Live/cached services inspected September 2026; RIVM acute-care 2026 v1.1
supports: Public-domain provider WMS/WFS at Epe's reference point returns Liander electricity (record updated 24 March 2026), Liander gas (17 December 2025), Vitens water and Ziggo media (both 7 September 2025); sewer/drainage returns no provider. Provider-supplied geometry has variable record dates and is responsibility context, not customer connectivity, pressure, capacity, quality, outage or restoration. Empty sewer territory is Unknown.

One NBNL/Partners in Energie sample postcode 8166GT maps to Liander service area OS VAASSEN 10-1i. It reports withdrawal existing/required/queue 42/40/6.6 MW with 30 queued requests and injection 63/36/30 MW with 26 requests; 27 projects have earliest year 2030. Capacity/project data updates at least quarterly and queues monthly; the product is open data but an exact licence identifier and frontend API stability are unstated. One postcode is not full coverage or outage telemetry.

RDI's statutory WFS assigns 79 antenna installations to GM0232, including 40 mobile-communication and 17 fixed-link sites. The public WFS states no reuse licence or guaranteed cadence. Sites do not establish operator ownership, coverage, backhaul, traffic, power/backup, damage or service availability.

RIVM's 2026 v1.1 acute-care questionnaire is CC0 and assigns no emergency department to GM0232. The nearest questionnaire location to the municipal centre is Gelre Ziekenhuizen Apeldoorn about 16.6 km straight-line, followed by Deventer Ziekenhuis about 17.1 km. These are dated offer records, not live acceptance, occupancy, staffing, generator endurance or road reachability.

DUO's daily API (complete around 06:15 Europe/Amsterdam) assigns 31 active education-location uses under CC BY with version unspecified. KVK/PDOK's Public Domain INSPIRE subset yields five government-service points inside the full boundary. Schools are not shelters and registered offices are not activated emergency facilities.

Simulation role is non-causal official context with affectsSimulation=false. Complete physical utility, care and supply topology or live state is unavailable or security-sensitive; use authorized operator feeds or an explicitly synthetic versioned fallback with uncertainty, never context-shaped false precision.

identity.summary: GM0232, Epe, Gelderland and Veiligheidsregio Noord- en Oost-Gelderland are internally and officially coherent.
notes: Generated municipality, regional bundle, province and exactly one safety-region assignment agree.
The context gate confirms centre [5.967725232909205, 52.33051875253281] lies inside the generated and fresh full 2025 boundary.
Boundary/statistics editions, fixed policy registers, timestamped observations and synthetic scenario time remain distinct.

geography.summary: The full boundary and places are coherent, but current local allocation contradicts the Veluwe forest and IJssel/Oene water geography.
notes: The full 2025 boundary has one component/ring and 2,363 positions; use it for source containment and hazard intersections rather than generalized overview geometry.

A controlled mixed-forest source in Buitengebied Vaassen ranks 23rd while Heggerenk ranks first, and Kern Oene ranks 25th in the persistent river scenario despite official IJssel/groundwater/dike evidence.
Representative points and a shared seed cannot substitute for terrain, connected flood footprints, catchments, eligible vegetation, wind, visitor locations, buildings, roads or control state.

demography.summary: Municipal controls and neighbourhood aggregates reconcile within CBS rounding semantics.
notes: CBS reports 33,469 residents; 29 neighbourhood rows sum to 33,475 (+6, +0.018%), while model detail reconciles exactly to 33,469.
Official controls are 9,046 residents aged 65+, 4,675 one-person households and 14,569 households; generated rows sum to 9,040, 4,675 and 14,570.
The 27.0% 65+ share is material, but age/residence is not a named need, care dependency, mobility limitation, cooling access or incident-time presence record.

regionalDetail.summary: Twenty-nine neighbourhoods support census allocation, but several fields and all physical/live infrastructure state remain incomplete.
notes: District-heating and public-charging fields are null in all 29 neighbourhoods; cars per household is missing in two and several housing/benefit fields are missing in one.
The public bundle adds 143 water assets, 79 antenna sites, 31 education uses, five government-service points and one electricity-capacity sample, each with different coverage and time semantics.
Null, suppressed, no returned provider, no assigned station, stale record, outside coverage and zero measured value are different states; none may be silently converted to zero or safe.

settlements.summary: BAG/BRT preserve Epe's four principal places and dispersed 24-label settlement pattern.
notes: The bundle contains Emst, Epe, Oene and Vaassen plus 19 buurtschappen and one gehucht, including Gortel, Tongeren, Wissel, Niersen, Vemde and Zuuk.
Settlement labels and CBS residents are reference geography, not holiday-park occupancy, day visitors, institutional population, warning reach or evacuation destinations.
Forest-adjacent hamlets/parks and eastern Oene require incident-specific access and exposure rather than interpolation from the municipal centre.

transport.summary: Six road proxies and 21 scheduled stop areas do not establish local evacuation, forest response, hospital access or T+72 mobility.
notes: A50/N-road boundary geometry omits local roads, bridges, culverts, the canal-side cycle-path failure mechanism, forest tracks and the two holiday-park clusters whose evacuation Epe says requires study.
There is no ProRail station inside GM0232. GTFS stop/schedule reference data, absence of an NDW match and an NWB edge do not prove a bus or road is operating, reachable or suitable for emergency use.

Current code correctly limits unqualified NWB edges to Mobility and explicitly assumed road-logistics/Supply; nominal 150/260 values are scenario units, not measured vehicles, evacuees, freight or repair throughput.

emergencyContext.summary: Official sources establish nature-fire, IJssel/brook, drought, weather and lifeline mechanisms, but no authority-approved incident, resource or action state drives output.
notes: Epe and VNOG make wildfire evacuation, residents/recreation users, care locations, extinguishing water, access and regional coordination explicit; the current wildfire preset does not model those local elements.
Water evidence distinguishes IJssel defences/seepage/Oene, brooks and culverts, Apeldoorns Kanaal/Grift, sewer/pump systems and drought inflow. None is selected as a hydraulic incident.

No confirmed shelter, distribution point, firefighting resource, local acute-care capacity, road restriction, warning action or utility restoration is integrated. Schools, antennas, offices, territories and questionnaires cannot be promoted to operational roles.
All ten hazards and eight services therefore remain exercises, not authority-validated forecasts or operational common operating picture.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at all six mandatory checkpoints for all eight services.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0232 pnpm audit:model passed one file/two tests in 45.30 seconds (45.08 seconds test time) after the artifact was written.

A private focused reproduction on current code passed one file/one test in 49.06 seconds and recorded 10 presets x 6 checkpoints x 8 services, local balances, route scope, ranks, exact-zero behavior, selected-layer invariance, fine-time peaks, causal labels and a controlled official BRT forest source.

At T+24 modeled severity / affected population-equivalent / cumulative local pre-network person-hours are storm 0.054821 / 6,604 / 88,787.128891; pluvial 0.135624 / 3,574 / 81,453.013892; river 0.981961 / 18,997 / 305,972.657278; coastal 0.036234 / 0 / 22,422.051582; heat 0.086631 / 1,830 / 71,679.168052.

At T+72 storm/pluvial/coastal/winter/earthquake/wildfire direct severity is zero, river remains 0.981961, heat 0.086631, cyber 0.056621 and compound 0.246330. Cumulative person-hours respectively are 218,719.247224; 166,945.531625; 1,174,119.930575; 79,456.128416; 168,470.190973; 421,621.577711; 480,315.665793; 46,926.655899; 137,001.631776; and 1,129,988.004095. Structural completion does not validate local physics.

Headless Chromium at 1440x900 and 390x844 selected GM0232, River flood, Mobility and T+24/T+72 without page/console/local-resource errors or horizontal overflow. Initial/model readiness was 971/785 ms, municipality switching 5,260/5,101 ms, T+24 model 358/416 ms and T+72 670/754 ms. Desktop map drilldown selected Kern Oene.

numericalInvariants.summary: Outputs are finite, bounded, deterministic, exact at zero intensity, selected-layer invariant and locally reconciled.
notes: Every scenario's zero-intensity run returns exact zero event hazard, affected population and cumulative deprived person-hours at all checked checkpoints.
Changing the selected display layer leaves hazard, pressure and affected-population outputs exactly identical.

Compound T+24 detail has 29 rows summing to 33,469 residents and 21,411 affected. Demand/delivered pairs are Power 35.758361/16.033137, Water 25.735349/11.088208, Drainage 19.623617/5.920937, Gas 31.788995/19.144324, Telecom 15.857468/4.421986, Mobility 24.777294/6.080152, Facilities 15.054617/5.898216 and Supply 19.574987/10.523542.
Maximum checked reconciliation error is 3.552713678800501e-15. Arithmetic consistency is not empirical accuracy.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Local allocation is not plausible for Veluwe fire, IJssel/Oene flooding, street-scale rain or heat vulnerability.
notes: Pluvial, coastal, heat and wildfire have exactly the same complete 29-neighbourhood order: Heggerenk, Enkweg, Krugerstraat Zuid, Buitengebied Epe Noord, Krugerstraat Noord and Oosterhof lead; Epe Centrum, Kern Oene, Buitengebied Emst, Buitengebied Epe West, Hoge Weerd and Vaassen Centrum are last.
A controlled BRT mixed-forest source near Gortel reaches direct-fire peak 0.340431 at T+11, but its containing Buitengebied Vaassen ranks 23rd and Heggerenk remains first.

River allocation changes only partially: Kern Oene remains 25th at local hazard 0.891805, while western Epe neighbourhoods occupy much of the top. Official evidence distinguishes Oene/IJssel influence, dikes, seepage, inflow and pump constraints.
No GM0232 unsupported-spatial dimension is emitted; compound reports unsupportedDimensions=[] despite these falsified allocations.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact eight-service availability exceeds verified local topology, capacity, state, backup and reachability evidence.
notes: At compound T+24 availability is Power 0.448374, Water 0.430855, Drainage 0.301725, Gas 0.602231, Telecom 0.278858, Mobility 0.245392, Facilities 0.391788 and Supply 0.537601.
There are zero modeled physical routes for Power, Water, Drainage, Gas, Telecom and Facilities; six NWB roads support Mobility and six support explicitly assumed road-logistics/Supply.

HWH objects, Liander/Vitens/Ziggo territories, one NBNL planning sample, 79 antenna sites, 31 education uses and RIVM/KVK facility points are non-causal context and cannot justify exact availability, dependencies or repair state.

No complete public live topology/state source was found. Use operator-authorized and security-safe data where available; otherwise label a minimal synthetic exercise graph, parameters and uncertainty and expose unavailable state as Unknown.

causalTrace.summary: Checked causal, population and service ledgers close arithmetically and identify model weights as assumptions.
notes: Compound output contains hazard, direct-service, interdependency, network, recovery and local-allocation records with matched totals.

Cumulative person-hours reconcile to a matched no-event local pre-network service baseline and explicitly exclude intermunicipal transfers. This is an accounting identity, not observed outage duration.

Explanations identify dimension shares and system-pressure weights as transparent deterministic assumptions, but no incident ID, official local hazard surface, provider topology, calibration, activated intervention or authority-approved resource state is attached.

Observed, forecast, static-context, historical/project, scenario and synthetic records need evidence class, issue/valid/retrieval time, spatial support, NoData and transformation lineage in UI and exports.

recovery72h.summary: Compound deterioration and river/facility behavior through T+72 lack incident-valid actions, resources, access or observations.
notes: Compound affected population-equivalent rises from 21,411 at T+24 to 21,657 at T+72 while severity falls 0.809967 to 0.246330. All services worsen: Power 0.448374 to 0.439206, Water 0.430855 to 0.428491, Drainage 0.301725 to 0.299708, Gas 0.602231 to 0.600777, Telecom 0.278858 to 0.272975, Mobility 0.245392 to 0.240763, Facilities 0.391788 to 0.388148 and Supply 0.537601 to 0.527782; all recovery remains zero.

River severity and seven service availabilities are fixed through T+72 with zero recovery while Facilities alone falls 0.536815 to 0.359477; no breach evolution, evacuation, hospital dependency, crew, access or facility event explains it.
Coastal T+72 exposes abstract recovery factors 0.487141-0.902919 and wildfire 0.755225-1.0 without named crews, routes, water, fuel, spares, completed actions or observed restoration.
Every improvement, plateau or deterioration must be traceable to a typed action/resource/dependency state with owner, prerequisites, valid time and uncertainty.

findings.summary: Wildfire allocation contradicts a controlled Veluwe forest source and omits resident, park, access and suppression geography.
findings.evidence: Epe/VNOG identify 7,109 ha of nature area, forest-adjacent homes, roads, care locations and many holiday parks, including evacuation concern at two park clusters and meetings at Gortel/Tongeren. A controlled source at [5.881675887977473, 52.30926841411657] inside official BRT mixed forest and Buitengebied Vaassen peaks at direct fire 0.340431 at T+11, but its source neighbourhood ranks 23rd of 29 while urban Heggerenk ranks first. The canonical preset itself has zero direct fire at T+24 and only generic smoke/drought effects.
findings.action: Mark GM0232 wildfire spatial output unsupported. Integrate BRT CC BY 4.0 eligible cover and dates, an authority-selected ignition/perimeter, fuel/moisture, timestamped KNMI wind, forest/park resident and visitor exposure, access/escape routes, extinguishing water and suppression state. Test source containment and keep land-cover geometry distinct from a live fire.

findings.summary: A generic centre-distance screen is presented as 3.14 m persistent local river flooding without a named IJssel hydraulic scenario.
findings.evidence: River severity 0.981961 and floodDepthM 3.142642 persist at T+24 and T+72, with affected population-equivalent 18,997 rising to 20,167, Drainage 0.195728, Mobility 0.277086 and no recovery. No failed dike section, water level, connected footprint, probability band, arrival or recession is selected. Kern Oene ranks 25th despite municipal evidence of IJssel-influenced high groundwater, dike seepage, constrained inflow, pump and water-system issues. The responsive UI headlines municipal Mobility as critical 28% at both checkpoints without an unsupported warning.
findings.action: Suppress exact depth/impact or label Unknown until VNOG/Waterschap experts select and version a LIWO/LDO scenario with source water, defence/breach, state, depth, arrival, duration and NoData. Intersect full 2025 geometry and relevant buildings/roads/assets; validate Oene and the eastern low area separately from western Veluwe high ground.

findings.summary: Pluvial allocation ignores Epe's named brooks, culverts, pumps, sewers, groundwater and street-scale constraints.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports flood stress 0.187787, 3,574 affected and 81,453.013892 person-hours but uses the same complete rank as coastal, heat and wildfire. Epe names Verloren Beek/Papenstraat, Schotweg, Gelriaweg, Epe-centre ponds, Oosterhof/Jonasweg and Oene constraints. The HWH snapshot exposes 143 local assets but none supplies current state or connectivity; the 2023 canal-embankment breach closed a cycle path yet did not inundate because the Grift handled flow.
findings.action: Integrate the native Epe 74 mm/1 h stress-test/hotspot layer after obtaining licence, edition, units and NoData, and compare with the CC0 RWS 70 mm/2 h WMS and AHN4 0.5 m DTM. Add versioned HWH catchments/defences/assets plus authorized sewer, pump, receiving-level and control state. Historical incidents validate mechanisms only, not automatic scenario failures.

findings.summary: Heat/drought output ignores older residents, forest/soil, water-availability and building differences and reuses the common spatial seed.
findings.evidence: Heat remains severity 0.086631 with drought 0.481283 through T+72; at T+24 it reports 1,830 affected and Water availability 0.627557. The rank is identical to pluvial/coastal/wildfire and places Epe Centrum and Hoge Weerd near the bottom. CBS gives 9,046 residents aged 65+ (27.0%); Epe notes many older residents in non-heat-adapted homes and prioritizes water shortage, vulnerable groups and forest drought. Current 2026 water restrictions and a remote KNMI station are not this exercise's T+72 forcing.
findings.action: Use a versioned KNMI forecast/heat/PET or surface-temperature layer with issue/valid time, shade/land cover, building characteristics and authority-approved vulnerability/cooling-resource data. Couple drought only to explicit water-source/level/demand assumptions; preserve current measures as observed context and keep drinking-water capacity Unknown without Vitens-authorized evidence.

findings.summary: All eight services deteriorate through T+72 while forcing falls and no recovery/action/resource state explains the trajectory.
findings.evidence: Compound severity falls 0.809967 to 0.246330 while affected population-equivalent grows 21,411 to 21,657 and person-hours 301,031.177666 to 1,129,988.004095. Power, Water, Drainage, Gas, Telecom, Mobility, Facilities and Supply all worsen between T+24 and T+72, and all recovery progress remains zero. No incident owner, crew, material, fuel, access, intervention, observation or facility/utility restoration state is attached.
findings.action: Require a typed incident and action/resource ledger with authority/owner, target, prerequisites, crew/material/fuel, access, start/end, state, observation time and uncertainty. Add T+0/6/12/24/48/72 tests requiring every deterioration, plateau or recovery to cite a causal state while preserving reconciliation and exact-zero input.

findings.summary: Exact eight-service availability has no verified physical utility/facility topology or live operator state.
findings.evidence: Compound T+24 exact availability ranges from Mobility 0.245392 to Gas 0.602231. Power, Water, Drainage, Gas, Telecom and Facilities have zero physical graph edges; six NWB routes support only Mobility and assumed road-logistics/Supply. Liander/Vitens/Ziggo territories, one NBNL postcode, 143 water assets, 79 antenna sites, 31 education uses and facility registers are context, not compatible topology, capacity, switching, pressure, backhaul, backup or restoration. Sewer provider lookup returns empty and must remain Unknown.
findings.action: Integrate authorized operator topology, outage, backup, priority-user and restoration feeds where security agreements permit. Preserve provider WMS Public Domain, HWH CC BY-SA, NBNL planning, RDI WFS, DUO daily and RIVM/KVK records as separately labelled non-causal context. Otherwise publish a minimal versioned synthetic exercise network with ranges/uncertainty rather than operator-validated-looking decimals.

findings.summary: Forest evacuation, dispersed settlements, public transport and external acute-care reachability are not modeled for the first 72 hours.
findings.evidence: GM0232 has 24 settlement labels, no ProRail station and 21 GTFS stops. Epe explicitly says evacuation feasibility of two holiday-park clusters needs study. RIVM assigns no emergency department inside the boundary; the two nearest questionnaire hospitals are roughly 16.6 and 17.1 km straight-line from the municipal centre. Six boundary roads omit local forest tracks, culverts, canal-side failures, bus operation, ambulance routing and incident-time access; no NDW record does not establish passability.
findings.action: Build an authority-reviewed multimodal access graph from monthly NWB, local road/bridge/culvert data and valid GTFS/operational feeds, with forest/park egress, response-water access and external hospital routes. Attach direction, capacity meaning, validity, closure, emergency priority and uncertainty; register care/shelter/distribution roles only with activation, capacity, accessibility, backup and owner state.

findings.summary: Storm, winter, cyber, earthquake and coastal outputs execute but remain uncalibrated or narrowly scoped.
findings.evidence: At T+24 storm reports 6,604 affected, winter 10,471 and cyber 10,459 with exact service effects but no selected warning/forecast, exposed-object layer or cyber target/system boundary. Earthquake peaks at T+2.25 with 0.021599 g without a selected event, GMPE, site response or fragility. Direct coastal water is correctly screened to zero locally but the scenario still accumulates 79,456.128416 person-hours through wind effects; zero direct water says nothing about indirect evacuee/supply demand or local non-coastal water pathways.
findings.action: Bind weather exercises to declared synthetic forcing or versioned KNMI observations/forecasts with issue/valid time and uncertainty; define cyber target, organization/system boundary and authorized dependencies. Require selected seismic event/source/GMPE/site/fragility before PGA or damage. Label coastal zero by its narrow direct-water scope and keep omitted indirect/local pathways Unknown.

findings.summary: Current observations, planning registers and absent local points need stronger temporal and NoData separation from the scenario clock.
findings.evidence: The deployment has no GM0232 Waterinfo, NDW, RIVM PM2.5, KNMI seismic or local KNMI-weather point and no Gelderland warning in its issued 48-hour window. Separately, WSVV's current drought liveblog describes restrictions and emergency pumping, NBNL reports planning queues/projects, and HWH/RDI/provider records carry varied update dates. None is a T+72 forecast or proof of zero hazard/service failure.
findings.action: Use an explicit evidence envelope on every record: evidence class, publisher, licence, observation/issue/valid/retrieval time, spatial support, cadence, quality, coverage and affectsSimulation. Render absent/expired/outside/stale as distinct Unknown states; permit causal use only after scenario-time alignment and a declared transformation.

findings.summary: A responsive workflow presents unsupported river mobility and local detail as decision-ready scenario state.
findings.evidence: Desktop/mobile required four controls from the default to GM0232, River flood, Mobility and T+24, then one more control for T+72; mobile also required opening details. Both views headline municipal Mobility as critical 28% at T+24/T+72 with 'Scenario · evidence class scenario' and no local spatial/hydraulic warning. Desktop drilldown selects Kern Oene and shows 46% at T+72 with precise causal bars although no named flood footprint exists. The inspector does disclose that network flow is a logical proxy and public layers are context, and both layouts had no errors or overflow, but the warning is not adjacent to the decision number.
findings.action: Gate exact availability/status and causal bars by municipality-hazard-service support. Put missing hydraulic footprint, local allocation, topology, recovery, valid-time and NoData warnings beside the hero and in exports; expose the narrow scope of direct/coastal zeros and separate municipal from selected-neighbourhood values. Keep controls responsive and preserve the current context caveats.

corrections.summary: Replace Epe's shared neighbourhood seed with source-aware, hazard-specific and support-gated spatial inputs.
corrections.validation: GM0232 wildfire, pluvial, river, heat and other local hazard families must expose unsupported/Unknown until calibrated. Use full 2025 geometry; BRT CC BY 4.0 land cover, AHN4 0.5 m CC0 terrain and event-specific footprints/weather. Assert that the controlled Buitengebied Vaassen forest source ranks in its affected footprint and that unrelated hazards do not silently share the complete 29-row order.

corrections.summary: Integrate selected IJssel/brook/cloudburst scenarios and public Epe water-system data with explicit NoData and operational-state boundaries.
corrections.validation: Use an expert-selected versioned LIWO/LDO footprint for river flooding and the native Epe stress-test raster for 74 mm/1 h after resolving licence/access; compare the RWS 70 mm/2 h CC0 layer without conflating events. Ingest HWH kering/zonering/catchment/object OGC under CC BY-SA with contributor coverage and registration time. Test Oene/IJssel connectivity, depth/arrival/recession and distinguish dry, no-data, no scenario and unavailable live state.

corrections.summary: Evidence-gate all eight lifelines and retain public provider/register/planning layers as non-causal context.
corrections.validation: For Power, Water, Drainage, Gas, Telecom, Mobility, Facilities and Supply separately require topology, compatible capacity unit, state, backup, restoration and uncertainty. Keep unqualified NWB excluded from six non-road graphs and restricted to Mobility/assumed road-logistics Supply. Provider WMS, HWH, NBNL, RDI, DUO, RIVM and KVK records must remain affectsSimulation=false absent authorized bindings; empty sewer/provider or point coverage displays Unknown.

corrections.summary: Make first-72-hour service evolution conditional on a traceable incident/action/resource ledger.
corrections.validation: At T+0/6/12/24/48/72 every deterioration, plateau and recovery must cite incident driver, authority/owner, action, prerequisite, crew/material/water/fuel, access, valid time, state and uncertainty. Specifically prevent GM0232's all-service compound worsening and river Facilities-only decline from appearing decision-grade without causes; retain arithmetic reconciliation and exact-zero input.

corrections.summary: Add Epe-specific evacuation, visitor, dispersed-settlement and external-care continuity context.
corrections.validation: Version monthly CC0 NWB, local roads/structures and valid transit feeds with non-additive corridor semantics; add authority-approved park/forest egress and external acute-care routes. Public GTFS, RIVM and DUO/KVK points remain candidates until activation/capacity/operation is known. Tests cover Gortel/Tongeren/park and Oene access under fire, flood, winter and compound conditions without converting no current NDW record to passable.

corrections.summary: Expose support, evidence time and NoData prominently in the operations UI and exports.
corrections.validation: At 1440x900 and 390x844, GM0232 River/Mobility T+24/T+72 and Kern Oene drilldown place missing footprint/topology/recovery and Unknown warnings beside exact numbers; municipal and neighbourhood scope are explicit. Current observations/warnings, static context, planning and scenario outputs display distinct evidence classes and times, remain operable without overflow/errors and never imply that no point/no warning means zero or safe.

residualLimitations: Complete physical electricity, gas, drinking-water, sewer/drainage, telecom, care and supply topology, switching/control logic, live load, damage, outage, crew, spare, water, fuel and repair state are unavailable or security-sensitive; no public geometry, territory or register can honestly replace them.

LIWO/LDO requires an expert-selected scenario and careful access/licence/version handling. A maximum-depth layer is not current water or a forecast, and NoData, no selected scenario and dry cells are different.

HWH exposes extensive Epe water geometry but national completeness is partial and object registration/status does not establish current condition, connectivity, flow, control setting, defence strength or backup power.

BRT forest, municipal hotspots and VNOG risk context are static/scenario evidence, not current fuel moisture, ignition, flame/smoke perimeter, visitor count, evacuation status or suppression resources.

CBS registered population omits incident-time visitors, holiday-park occupancy, workers and institutional presence. Rounded/suppressed aggregates cannot identify individuals, mobility limits or care needs.

NWB/GTFS/NDW and RIVM points do not establish scenario-time road/transit operation, emergency priority, hospital acceptance or route capacity. Absence of a local station, record or facility class is not zero service or safety.

Current model numbers remain synthetic exercise outputs. They must not be described as observed, forecast, operator-validated or decision-grade until the critical/high findings are corrected and authorities accept the scenario.
provinceReviewFlags: Gelderland/VNOG review should establish one Veluwe nature-fire evidence contract covering eligible land cover, fuel/moisture, event-valid wind, ignition/perimeter, visitors/parks/care, access/escape routes, extinguishing water, resources and suppression without treating BRT or zoning geometry as a live fire.

Gelderland and Vallei en Veluwe should standardize expert selection/versioning of IJssel LIWO/LDO scenarios and Oene/eastern-area validation, including defence/breach, water level, connected depth, arrival, recession and NoData semantics.

Province, water board and Epe should publish or agree a reusable machine route for the municipal 74 mm/1 h stress-test and named hotspot register, with licence, edition, CRS, units, rainfall duration, antecedent conditions and explicit no-data meaning.
VNOG municipalities need a shared first-72-hour park/recreation, rural settlement, external acute-care and road-access data contract that separates candidate geometry from activated capacity/state.

Gelderland review should govern provider/HWH/NBNL/RDI/RIVM/DUO/KNMI/RWS evidence classes and time alignment so current observations, registers and planning context cannot be promoted to scenario or T+72 truth.
